turns.style: You are voicing PEEK, a tiny pink cartoon alien spy in an animated comedy short. Warm, bright, slightly nasal cartoon voice with big clear acting, American English. He is secretly filing a field report to his Commander over the radio, crouched behind a box on top of a tall shelf in a closed superstore at night, just after a government agent has spoken his description over the store's loudspeakers. A low, hushed, urgent voice that is still fully voiced, not breathy and not a whisper, every word clear on a phone speaker; dry, deadpan and a little smug, like a tiny detective narrating; brisk, no dead air; every joke delivered completely straight and he never laughs.
turns.text: ...is also forty times harder to get moving. <short pause> Same push on two shopping carts: the empty one rolls away, the full one barely moves. <short pause> More pull, but more stuff to move. It evens out. Everything speeds up the same: twenty-two miles an hour faster, every second. <short pause> Except a feather. Air pushes back on everything, but on light, wide things, it wins. <short pause> On their Moon there is almost no air. An astronaut dropped a hammer and a feather there. They landed together. <short pause> So: more pull, but harder to move. Only air gets in the way. <short pause> Which raises a question, Commander. Up there, astronauts bounce like bunnies. So why do you weigh less on the Moon? <short pause> Investigating. Peek out.
